conditions: Windows, installed Chrome headless, next start production build, owned loopback PostgreSQL 17.11 disposable cluster, schema-only fixture, real Better Auth email OTP to a loopback stand-in, no route interception

steps.name: a real client signs in on the disposable cluster
the clean profile renders no image and offers the initials
the legacy value is written into the record the server serves
the profile page hides a dead preview address and says nothing about a saved photo
steps.error:
the page painted a dead address as a photo: {"present":true,"hasImage":true,"src":"blob:http://127.0.0.1:59991/0000dead-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","complete":true,"naturalWidth":0,"text":"","fallback":false}

true !== false

steps.name: a real address in the same record still shows the photo
a photo the server will not take is reported as a failure, not as a saved picture
the profile journey adds no client-side errors

samples.sheetText: Review your photo Image uploads are not available in this environment yet. Try a different photo Retry upload

notes: the upload route answered 403 to a post with no file, which is the server-side refusal this step depends on, not a client-side guess.

the legacy values are written into identity_workspaces.profile (the record /api/me serves for a session that has a workspace) and read back from that endpoint before the page is reloaded, so the page is refusing a value the server really serves, not one the harness withheld.
users.profile_image_url is only served by /api/me when the session has no active workspace, and the app does not produce such a signed-in session, so that fallback branch is not measured here.

the real address is a file the app itself serves, so the "still shows the photo" step reads the decoded width rather than only the attribute. No third-party host is reached: the route filter aborts everything off loopback.

uploads are disabled server-side in this build, so the picker step measures the honest failure path. The companion guard for a server that answers 200 with a preview address is covered by tests/image-editor-truthfulness.cjs, which injects that response.
this drives the client profile card. The provider card uses the same helper but is not signed in here; it stays a code-level guard until a provider session is run.
